title: Soil
author: Wikipedia contributors
attribution: Wikipedia contributors, “Soil”, English Wikipedia. Text available under CC BY-SA 4.0; see source history for contributors.
paragraphs: Soil, also commonly referred to as earth, is a mixture of organic matter, minerals, gases, water, and organisms that together support the life of plants and soil organisms. Some scientific definitions distinguish dirt from soil by restricting the former term specifically to displaced soil.

Soil consists of a solid collection of minerals and organic matter (the soil matrix), as well as a porous phase (Pore space) that holds gases (the soil atmosphere) and a liquid phase that holds water and dissolved substances both organic and inorganic, in ionic or in molecular form (the soil solution). Accordingly, soil is a complex three-state system of solids, liquids, and gases. Soil is a product of several factors: the influence of climate, relief (elevation, orientation, and slope of terrain), organisms, and the soil's parent materials (original minerals) interacting over time. It continually undergoes development through numerous physical, chemical, and biological processes, which include weathering with associated erosion. Given its complexity and strong internal connectedness, soil ecologists regard soil as an ecosystem.

Most soils have a dry bulk density (density of soil taking into account voids when dry) between 1.1 and 1.6 g/cm3, though the soil particle density is much higher, in the range of 2.6 to 2.7 g/cm3. Little of the soil of planet Earth is older than the Pleistocene and none is older than the Cenozoic, although fossilized soils are preserved from as far back as the Archean.
Collectively, the Earth's body of soil is called the pedosphere. The pedosphere interfaces with the lithosphere, the hydrosphere, the atmosphere, and the biosphere. Soil has four important functions:
as a medium for plant growth
as a means of water storage, water supply, and water purification
as a modifier of Earth's atmosphere
as a habitat for soil organisms
All of these functions, in their turn, modify the soil and its properties.

Soil science has two basic branches of study: edaphology and pedology. Edaphology studies the influence of soils on living things. Pedology focuses on the formation, description (morphology), and classification of soils in their natural environment. In engineering terms, soil is included in the broader concept of regolith, which also includes other loose material that lies above the bedrock, as can be found on the Moon and other celestial objects.

sentence.text: Given its complexity and strong internal connectedness, soil ecologists regard soil as an ecosystem.
sentence.translation: 考虑到土壤的复杂性和其内部紧密的相互联系，土壤生态学家将其视为一个生态系统。
sentence.analysis: Given 在句首用作介词，意为“考虑到”，引出作背景依据的名词短语；its 指 soil。主干是 soil ecologists regard soil as an ecosystem。regard A as B 是“将 A 视为 B”的结构，as 后的 an ecosystem 补充说明宾语 soil 的身份。

questions.question: Why do soil ecologists regard soil as an ecosystem?
options: Because it is complex and strongly interconnected internally
Because it contains only living organisms
Because all soils have exactly the same density
Because it is isolated from the atmosphere
questions.explanation: 第二段以 Given its complexity and strong internal connectedness 明确给出理由。第一、二段还表明土壤含有矿物、水和气体，并非只有生物。

questions.question: Which topic belongs specifically to pedology as described in the passage?
options: Only the effects of soil on living things
The formation and classification of soils in their natural environment
Only the chemistry of ocean water
The design of artificial plant lighting
questions.explanation: 第十段对照两分支：edaphology 研究土壤对生物的影响；pedology 关注 formation、description 和 classification。应根据学科与研究对象的对应关系作答。
